---
title: "How to load compressed LFP"
---

This guide downloads and loads the **full-recording compressed LFP** archives produced by
[lfpack](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/lfpack). They are lossy HDF5 encodings of the
entire LFP trace for every insertion (release **v04**, 1099 insertions), at three tiers.

Unlike the [cells aggregates](load-cells-features.qmd), which hold short per-cell
snippets, these are the **whole recording**, decompressed on demand.

::: {.callout-important}
These archives are in a private S3 bucket and need an IBL account — pass a logged-in
[`one.api.ONE`](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ONE/) instance.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Reading v04 (lfpack format 2) requires **`lfpack>=1.0.0`**. The v03 archives and their
`mild` / `aggressive` levels are removed: asking for either level raises `ValueError`.
`small` replaces `mild`.
:::

## Tiers

All tiers use the same codec (ε = 100). They differ only in α, the wavelet-packet
threshold, which is the only parameter that moves decoding:

| `level` | α | File | Size | File / float32 at 250 Hz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `small` | 14 | `lf_compressed_v04_a14_small_all.h5` | 11.2 GB | 0.57 % |
| `default` | 7 | `lf_compressed_v04_a07_default_all.h5` | 21.5 GB | 1.10 % |
| `fine` | 2.5 | `lf_compressed_v04_a2p5_fine_all.h5` | 46.1 GB | 2.35 % |

Use `default` unless size matters (`small`, which decodes like the former v03 `mild` at a
third of the size) or fidelity matters (`fine`).

Every recording carries its brain locations (`ml` / `ap` / `dv` / `atlas_id` /
`acronym`), sync knots, bad-channel `labels` and a saturation table.

Known exceptions: insertion `bf96f6d6` has no bad-channel labels, and two insertions are
fully flagged bad and decode to zeros
([lfpack#21](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/lfpack/issues/21)).

## S3 layout

```text
aggregates/atlas/projects/{project}/
│
└── lfp_aggregates/
    ├── lf_compressed_v04_a14_small_all.h5     small   (ε=100, α=14)   ~11 GB
    ├── lf_compressed_v04_a07_default_all.h5   default (ε=100, α=7)    ~21.5 GB
    └── lf_compressed_v04_a2p5_fine_all.h5     fine    (ε=100, α=2.5)  ~46 GB
```

Each archive is a single multi-recording HDF5 file with one top-level group per insertion
(`pid`), produced by `lfpack.merge_h5`.

## Download

```python
from pathlib import Path

from one.api import ONE
import ephysatlas.data

one = ONE(base_url="https://alyx.internationalbrainlab.org")
local_path = Path("/datadisk/ephys-atlas")
project = "ibl_neuropixel_brainwide_01"

# default tier (~21.5 GB)
ephysatlas.data.download_lfp_features(local_path, project=project, one=one)

# small tier (~11 GB)
ephysatlas.data.download_lfp_features(
    local_path, project=project, one=one, level="small"
)
```

## Load

```python
from pathlib import Path

import ephysatlas.data

local_path = Path("/datadisk/ephys-atlas")
project = "ibl_neuropixel_brainwide_01"
pid = "00a824c0-e060-495f-9ebc-79c82fef4c67"

sr = ephysatlas.data.read_lfp_features(local_path / project, pid)   # level="default"

traces = sr[0:2500, :]   # (2500, nc) float32, volts
print(sr.nc, sr.fs)      # channel count, sample rate (Hz)
```

`read_lfp_features` returns an `lfpack.LFPackReader`, a **drop-in replacement for
`spikeglx.Reader`**. Slicing decompresses only the chunks you ask for, so the full
recording never enters memory — the 21.5 GB default archive is usable on a laptop.

## Reducing what you read

Two arguments cut the cost of a read:

```python
# Sum adjacent channels on read: 384 channels -> 96 spatial bins
sr = ephysatlas.data.read_lfp_features(
    local_path / project, pid, bin_channels=4
)

# Open a coarser pyramidal level
sr = ephysatlas.data.read_lfp_features(local_path / project, pid, scale=1)

# Another tier, if that is what you downloaded
sr = ephysatlas.data.read_lfp_features(
    local_path / project, pid, level="small"
)
```

`bin_channels` is the one to reach for when sweeping across many recordings: adjacent
channels are strongly correlated at LFP frequencies, so binning by 4 keeps depth
resolution useful while quartering the memory.

## Computing features from the archives

`LFPackFeatureCalculator` computes the `lf` and `csd` feature families straight from an
archive. The LF in the archive is already high-pass filtered, common-average referenced,
bad-channel interpolated, decimated to about 250 Hz and Cadzow-denoised, so tell the
pipeline not to do it again: skip LF destriping, and skip the decimation and denoising
before the CSD.

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import (
    CsdParams,
    FeatureComputationOptions,
    FeatureParams,
    LFPackFeatureCalculator,
)

options = FeatureComputationOptions(
    features_to_compute=["lf", "csd"],
    skip_lf_destripe=True,                                   # no destriping
    feature_params=FeatureParams(
        csd=CsdParams(decimate=1, denoise=False)             # no CSD decimation or denoising
    ),
)

calc = LFPackFeatureCalculator(
    local_path / project / "lfp_aggregates" / "lf_compressed_v04_a07_default_all.h5",
    recording=pid,   # the archive holds every recording: pick one by its pid
)
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(
    n_snippets=5, duration_ap=0.0, duration_lf=5.0, options=options
)
print(df.index.names)   # ['pid', 'channel']
```

Without `skip_lf_destripe=True`, destriping fails on the 250 Hz data with
`ValueError: Digital filter critical frequencies must be 0 < Wn < fs/2`. The result has
only the `lf` and `csd` families, so the published region models, which need all four,
cannot run on it. [Tune the computation](tune-feature-computation.qmd) covers single
snippets and choosing the snippet windows.

## Working with lfpack directly

`read_lfp_features` is a convenience wrapper that resolves the archive path for you. For
anything beyond opening a recording — session-clock timestamps, saturation quality
control, embedded per-channel brain regions, listing the recordings in an archive — use
`LFPackReader` directly and see the
[lfpack documentation](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/lfpack/), which documents this
dataset in depth.
